deviation_mechanism: The persistence of Cr thickness near 200 nm stems from the physical nature of metal film optics in the thick-film limit. At ~200 nm, chromium acts as a bulk absorber where the optical penetration depth is fully exceeded, heavily damping the internal electric field and flattening the objective function's gradient with respect to thickness variations. This creates a low-sensitivity region in the parameter space where gradient-based or population-search updates receive negligible directional feedback, preventing rapid convergence toward the 5-30 nm window where thin-film interference and field localization dominate the transfer-matrix response.
